# SEO-033: Emit exactly one non-empty title element per page

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `metadata` |

| Impact | `LOW` |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Every indexable HTML response contains one title element inside head whose text content is neither empty nor an unreplaced template placeholder, and no response contains a second title element.

## Rationale

The title element is the primary label a result listing has for a page, so when it is absent, empty, or duplicated the engine constructs a label from whatever other text it finds and the site loses control of how the page is named.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Locate the single layer that owns the document head for each route and set the title there. If the framework merges a layout title with a route title, confirm the merged result yields one element rather than one per layer, and remove any hardcoded fallback that survives into production.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Count title elements in the head of the served response for a sample of routes and record the text content of each one found.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `RAW_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `title-element-single`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`, `SOCIAL_PREVIEW`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
